name: worktree-write-scope-decisions
body:
Worktree-only write scope for code-writer agents deepens `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`. Model: every generated code-writer agent's permission.edit grants target the worktree mirror `apg/.worktrees/*/` rather than a repo-root path. opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form reaches the worktree, and a root grant makes main writable. Law set: `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`, `requirements.requirement.agent-fs-write-operations`, `domain.value.permission-scope`, and `domain.constraint.fs-operation-scope-enforced` encode the worktree-only model. `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes` plus `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`, `domain.constraint.worktree-only-write-scope`, `domain.entity.worktree-write-boundary`, and `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` carry the scoped law. fs scope resolution: `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` resolves a candidate against the caller directory, and `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs` supplies the effective permission.edit scope (ALLOW and DENY, LAST match wins), so the fs tools read ALLOW and DENY rules, ordered, rather than allow globs alone. The code-writer requirement's acceptance criteria carry the single-frame rule and the main-resolving-path refusal. Scope is decided in one frame: the candidate path resolves to an absolute path against the session workspace root (the main-checkout root opencode uses) and matches grants anchored at that root, so an absolute path outside `
/apg/.worktrees/

/` is refused. Navigator git grant: the navigator frontmatter grants `git rebase *`, and the read-only verbs are `git status`/`diff`/`log`/`branch`. The exact read-only set is `git status *`, `git log *`, `git branch --show-current`, `git remote -v`, `git remote show *`, `git ls-files *`; the blanket `git branch *` and `git remote *` admit ref-writing and config-mutating forms and are excluded. `git rebase *` is pattern-cwd-agnostic, so the inside-the-worktree rule is prose-enforced, recorded in `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only`. The `git diff *`/`git log *` pair is additionally constrained by the `--output=` file-writing form recorded in `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only` (see `requirements.note.git-file-write-options-reconciled`). Release-agent: releases run from MAIN, so the release-agent's write grants target the main checkout; it is one of the two agent carve-outs of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` and carries zero worktree mirror. Its main-write set is repo-specific: the agent-builder analyses the repo (version files, packaging formulae, changelog, release scripts) and recommends the set, confirmed through the coordinator interview like build gates and test tiers; the spec fixes the policy alone. The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts regenerated by the agent-builder on main after a release, as `requirements.note.fix-regeneration-timing-after-release` states.
